=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves attach at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired leaves at same node visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves spaced out along the stem, not clustered at nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, serrate (margins show fine, irregular teeth along the edge, especially visible in close-up views)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest at or near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf base is broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off at angles)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, 6-8 pairs per leaf (secondary veins are distinct and run parallel to each other, curving toward the margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy, especially on upper surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface; surface smooth)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, less than half the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody; typical of young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is green with slight reddish-brown tinge in some areas, especially near nodes)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth, no visible ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate seen when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; pulvinus not visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible on any part of the seedling)
F. Notes: Some leaves show minor damage (small holes and light discoloration), likely due to environmental exposure or minor abrasion. The seedling is marked with a pink tag and white label (TEOPRA 2), which is not a biological feature. The images show the same individual from multiple angles; all observations are consistent across views. No evidence of flowering or fruiting structures.
